headline: Standardized benchmarks probe generalization of ML models in perturbation biology
label: Benchmarking Ml Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Large-scale public assays and leakage audits are testing whether predictive models generalize beyond their training contexts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is standardized, multi-dataset benchmarking of ML models for single-cell and biomolecular prediction. scArchon evaluates nine single-cell perturbation response tools across six scRNA-seq datasets within a modular Snakemake framework, while SigBridgeR unifies eight phenotype-associated cell screening algorithms with benchmarking across four cancer settings. Generalization is the central test: Mechanisms Matter reports that deep models often fail to transport across perturbation contexts, using a semi-synthetic Perturb-seq simulator. AssayBench scores LLMs and agents on 1,920 public CRISPR screens by adjusted nDCG, where LLMs outperform biology-specific models. What is new is the extension of this comparison to LLM-based and agentic workflows, including scHilda and S2F-agent, and to large assay collections rather than single tasks.
